newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI pushes down rupee against forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: India RBI pushes down rupee against forward dollar.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday intervened aggressively to weaken the rupee against the forward dollar but its intervention in the spot market was ineffective in the face of large capital inflows, dealers said.

The RBI bought forward dollars across wide maturities ranging from August-end to December and January, pushing up premiums by as much as 10 paise, the sharpest rise seen in recent months, dealers said.
January dollars touched a high of 78/81 paise on Monday, up from the opening level of 69/71 paise, dealers said.
The six-month annualised premium closed the day at 4.42 percent, up from the previous close of 3.85 percent.
A finance ministry announcement of a 30-billion-rupee auction of government stock at the close of trading buttressed the bullish sentiment on the forward dollar, dealers said.

RBI bought spot dollars also, but this had no impact in the face of a large inflow of $150 million -- raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation through its recent FRN issue -- sold by a handful of foreign banks, dealers said.
The spot rupee closed at 35.730/740 a dollar, stronger than Monday's opening level of 35.77/79, dealers said.
The rupee saw a high of 35.73 and a low of 35.77 on Monday.

"RBI's strategy to weaken the spot rupee appears to have been defeated," said a dealer at a European bank, referring to RBI's spot purchases which, coming on the top of corporate dollar demand, helped push down the rupee on Friday.

But some dealers said it was too early to pronounce a judgement. "You don't see $150 million inwards every day," said a dealer. But many dealers said RBI's strategy to push up forward dollar premiums may not be sustained for very long.
"The RBI governor said monetary policy would be aimed at achieving lower interest regime," said a dealer.
"And inflation is coming down." Pushing up premiums in this scenario would not be possible, he said.

For the first time during the current phase of rupee bouyancy, the commerce minister in New Delhi on Monday told a seminar the overvalued rupee was among the reasons contributing to a slowdown in Indian exports.
